what_it_does: Training very large AI models requires thousands of GPUs working in lockstep, and two things routinely cause efficiency to collapse: hardware failures that go unnoticed for too long (so GPUs sit idle while software waits for a timeout), and network congestion where multiple streams of "synchronization traffic" — the periodic all-machine summations that keep every GPU's model copy up to date — collide and queue up. The C4 system attacks both problems by exploiting the highly regular, repetitive structure of training workloads. Because every training iteration does essentially the same communication steps in the same order, an anomalously slow or failed component produces a recognizable symptom in the timing of these communications; C4 detects this quickly and reroutes or restarts before a software timeout fires. For the congestion problem, because the synchronization flows are few and predictable, C4 plans their routes in advance so they never share the same network link at the same time.
